coverage_notes:
PRIMARY SOURCE: the official 1992 University of Alabama Football Media Guide, scanned on the Internet Archive (https://archive.org/details/alabama-football-1992-media-guide-c). All quotes are copied byte-exact from the item's OCR text file at https://archive.org/download/alabama-football-1992-media-guide-c/Alabama%20Football%2C%201992%20Media%20Guide%20%28C%29_djvu.txt and were each programmatically verified as literal substrings of that file. Multi-line quotes preserve the file's actual newlines; the OCR reproduces the guide's section headers with a leading "@" or "H"/"I" glyph (the printed square bullet), which I left intact rather than normalizing.

WHAT I RECOVERED IN FULL: the head coach and all nine full-time on-field assistants (the NCAA limit at the time), from the guide's "THE COACHES" / "ON-THE-FIELD COACHES" section (guide pages 63-70). Both strength-and-conditioning coaches, both graduate assistants, three operations staffers, the equipment director, the head athletic trainer, five team physicians, and three football secretaries all come from the guide's "SUPPORT STAFF" section (guide pages 70-73).

TITLE CAVEAT (important): the 1992 media guide does not use the words "offensive coordinator" or "defensive coordinator" for anyone. Mal Moore is titled "Assistant Head Coach/Quarterbacks" and Bill Oliver is titled "Secondary". I kept those as the source-worded roles and attached secondary sources (Wikipedia's infobox for Moore as offensive coordinator; a CBS Sports obituary for Oliver as defensive coordinator) so the coordinator function is documented without me overwriting the primary source's wording.

OCR GAPS I WORKED AROUND: the archive's OCR dropped four on-field coaches' name headers (Jim Fuller, Ellis Johnson, Larry Kirksey, Danny Pearman) because they are set in a display typeface. For those four I cite the guide's all-time coaching roster (page 265, which lists tenure years and confirms each was on staff in 1992) plus the guide's own index entry pointing to their bio page, and I read the role off the rendered page scan. Their roles, read directly from the scanned pages: Fuller = Offensive Guards and Centers (p. 67), Johnson = Outside Linebackers (p. 67), Kirksey = Offensive Backs (p. 68), Pearman = Offensive Tackles (p. 69). Secretary Debbie Gibson's name is dropped entirely by the OCR (the caption is column-interleaved), so her row carries quote:"" per instructions; she is plainly legible in the page-73 scan. Mary Spybey's and Linda Knowles's caption text is likewise split across interleaved columns, so their quotes are short fragments of that caption.

TIERS I COULD NOT RECOVER:
- ANALYSTS and QUALITY CONTROL: none exist. These staff tiers did not exist in 1992 college football under then-current NCAA staff limits, and the media guide documents no such positions. Zero rows is the correct answer here, not a coverage failure.
- ADDITIONAL GRADUATE ASSISTANTS: only two are documented (Chip Davis, Mark Graham), pictured as headshots under a "Graduate Assistants" heading with no bios, no position assignments, and no other names. Programs of this era typically carried more student/volunteer assistants than they printed; any others are unrecoverable from published sources.
- ASSISTANT ATHLETIC TRAINERS and STUDENT TRAINERS: not named anywhere in the guide. Only head trainer Bill McDonald is listed.
- ASSISTANT EQUIPMENT STAFF and STUDENT MANAGERS: not named. Only director Tank Conerly is listed.
- ADDITIONAL S&C ASSISTANTS/INTERNS: not named beyond Caruthers and Terry Jones.

DELIBERATE EXCLUSIONS (documented, but not football team staff — listing them so the omission is auditable, not hidden): the same media-guide page 73 photo montage also names the Bryant Hall Grounds Crew (Willie Thompson, James Walker, Becky Logan), the Bryant Hall Dining Hall Directors (Loretta Clements, Dorothy Woods, Joanna Jackson), the Bryant Hall Dining Hall Staff (Marie Harris, Phillis Wills, Bertha Mathews, Celeste Hill, Leola Tinker, Ethel Mae Holloway, Ronnie Harris, Elizabeth Ryan, Lucinda Stewart, Charlotte Furr, Sharon Davis), the Bryant-Denny Stadium Grounds Crew (John Smalley, William Hendrix, Terry Cook, Lynn Laycock, Wayne Gilliland, Leslie Kelly), and the Alabama State Troopers assigned to Stallings (Captain Mike Sullivan, Cary Sutton). These are athletic-department facility, dining, and security personnel serving all sports and the stadium, not football team staff, so I left them out of the rows rather than inflating a ring count. Donald Rawson (Video Director) appears only in the guide's department-wide athletic directory, not the football staff section, so he is also excluded.

MIDSEASON CHANGES: none found. I searched contemporary coverage for any 1992 in-season arrival or departure and found nothing; every person listed was on staff from preseason through the January 1, 1993 Sugar Bowl. The one timing note worth flagging is Danny Pearman, who was promoted from graduate assistant to full-time on-field coach on April 15, 1992 — that is preseason, not midseason, so it does not affect the ring rule, but I recorded it on his row for transparency.

SOURCE-CHAIN NOTE: the requested Wayback Machine path was attempted and largely failed. rolltide.com's archived 1992 roster PDF (rolltide.com/documents/2010/4/21/92-m-footbl-roster.pdf) returns a single-page-app HTML shell in every Wayback capture, not a PDF. The archived official season PDF (s3.amazonaws.com/rolltide.com/documents/2016/8/18/1992_season.pdf, captured 2021-12-03) does download as a real 18 MB PDF but is a pure page-image scan with no text layer and no staff listing. A school athletics staff directory did not exist on the web in 1992. Wikipedia's team-season page is thin: its infobox names only Stallings and Moore, its roster footer names only Ellis Johnson, and its bottom navbox omits Woody McCorvey and Jeff Rouzie entirely — so the media guide is doing nearly all the work here.
